_comment: Auth context v1 — the shared truth table for what a valid capability is. Read by BOTH src/agento/toolbox/tests/auth-context-fixture.test.js (Node deriveAuthContext, the verifier) and tests/unit/framework/test_auth_context_fixture.py (Python derive_auth_context, the issuer). Timestamps are epoch seconds. `source` is what the source checker returned for the row (null = revoked/ended/unknown). `expected` null means rejected. A divergence is fail-open on one side, so the table lives in one file. E2/E6 mint from this shape; see docs/architecture/auth-context.md. `table_rows` holds the E1.5 framework-table rows (user, session, launch, role_grant), read by tests/integration/test_platform_foundation_schema.py and, for version ids, by the Node suite.

ttl_resolution.why: workspace row narrows the default row
workspace row may also widen within the ceiling
ENV wins over the workspace row
capability_ttl above the ceiling is clamped
session_max_ttl above the ceiling is clamped
launch_max_ttl above the ceiling is clamped
config.json above the ceiling is clamped too
unparsable value is an error, not a fallback
empty string is an error, not absent
boolean in config.json is an error

cases.why: mcp_job with a job id past 2^53 keeps every digit
mcp_job may carry its execution id
internal_rest with a view at module REST
internal_rest with a view at scoped /health
internal_rest with a POSITIVE job id (discovery flow, consumer.py) is accepted
backfilled internal_rest carries the legacy subject constant
miniapp with an integer version id
miniapp with an empty version id
miniapp with a version id over 64 characters
user_session with an integer user id upstream
mismatched job: user_session carrying a job
mismatched job: miniapp carrying a job
mismatched agent_view (row scoped, session is not)
agent_view whose workspace cannot be joined
internal_rest subject outside the service namespace
user_session pointing at a launch source
session source of the wrong kind
miniapp capability beyond the launch's end
user_session capability beyond the session's end

table_rows._comment: E1.5 framework tables: one row per case, inserted by tests/integration/test_platform_foundation_schema.py against the migrated schema; `valid` is whether MySQL accepts it. `@user`, `@workspace`, `@agent_view` are ids the test creates; `@missing` is an id that does not exist. A row the DB accepts is not always a row the reader may trust: see the role_grant scope cases. The Node suite asserts every version id here is a VA version id (paths.js VERSION_ID_RE).

user.why: no role: there is no default

launch.why: launch at workspace scope, with an exchange code

role_grant.why: both scopes: the DB accepts it, a reader must treat it as no grant
no scope: the DB accepts it, a reader must treat it as no grant
